suite.result: 51 pass / 0 fail / 499 expect() calls across 10 files
suite.generation3Rerun: 30 pass / 0 fail / 255 expect() calls after 5 re-points (see repointedCases); before re-pointing it was 25 pass / 5 fail, every failure being an expectation that encoded a now-fixed defect or the added lifetime field.
suite.repoSuiteReceipt: bun test packages/gateway at b83ad30: 134 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail / 572 expect() calls (leader receipt was 133 pass; b83ad30 added a redaction-calibration test).
suite.note: Every assertion encodes the OBSERVED behaviour of b83ad30, including the five defects below, so a green suite documents them rather than hiding them.

cases.angle: Task 1 baseline: the four values 0-Main reported leaking under the old 2-class gate.
cases.expectedBehavior: secret=deadbeefcafe, secret=ABCDEFGHIJKL, token=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx and secret=1234567890123456 are all redacted.
cases.observedBehavior: All four now redact to '<key>=[redacted]'. The old gate's 2-character-class requirement was the leak; b83ad30 removed it.

cases.angle: Task 1: make the gate MISS a real secret — 12-char all-lowercase, all-uppercase, purely numeric, 11-char, lowercase-only base64, and exactly 12 chars of one class.
cases.expectedBehavior: Every one of those shapes is redacted; the only survivor is below the declared 12-char floor.
cases.observedBehavior: REDACTED: api_key=abcdefghijkl, api_key=ABCDEFGHIJKL, password=123456789012, api_key=123456789012345678901234, api_key=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx, token=qqqqqqqqqqqq, token=QQQQQQQQQQQQ, token=111111111111, token=------------, api_key: "abcdefghijkl". Also redacted in the header form: 'Authorization: Bearer abcdefghijkl' and 'Authorization: Bearer 123456789012'. The only misses are BELOW the floor: token=Abcdefghij1 (11) and secret=deadbeefca1 (11) ship verbatim — the documented boundary, not a hole, and 11-char provider keys are not a real shape.

cases.angle: Task 1 (redirected by 0-Main): the NON_SECRET_KEY denylist is now the whole discriminator — smuggle a real 26-char credential behind an exempt word.
cases.expectedBehavior: A credential-shaped value is redacted regardless of what else the key name happens to contain.
cases.observedBehavior: LEAK, 18/18 attempts. Every one of these delivers the secret verbatim to the chat surface: max_token=, max_secret=, MAX_TOKEN=, AWS_MAX_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=, auth_expires_secret=, expired_password=, retries_token=, token_ttl_secret=, count_api_key=, age_token=, ms_token=, num_credential=, total_authorization=, remaining_secret=, window_passwd=, attempt_token=, seconds_apikey=, and the quoted form max_token: "<secret>". Confirmed end to end: formatFailureNotice for expired_password=deadbeefcafebabe0123456789 contains the secret. A word that merely CONTAINS an exempt word (maximal_token, message_token, damage_token) is correctly NOT exempt, which is the only thing keeping the hole from being wider.

cases.angle: Task 1: the denylist is matched against the captured prefix, whose affix class is [A-Za-z0-9_] only.
cases.expectedBehavior: Whether a key is exempt should not depend on the separator an operator or a runtime happened to use.
cases.observedBehavior: It does. 'max-tokens=200000000000' -> 'max-tokens=[redacted]' (over-redacted) while 'max_tokens=200000000000' survives; 'max_token=<26-char secret>' leaks while 'limit-token=<same secret>' redacts. A dash immediately after the key word ('max-token-limit=/var/log/gateway-quota.log') breaks the assignment match entirely and nothing is redacted or reported.

cases.angle: Task 2: file paths, UUIDs, session ids, git SHAs, stack frames and JSON blobs that are NOT the value of an auth-ish key.
cases.expectedBehavior: All survive byte-for-byte.
cases.observedBehavior: All ten survive unchanged, including a two-frame stack trace with real paths, a ULID + sha256 pair, 'max_tokens=200000', 'oauth: exchange rejected', 'token_expires_at=2026-08-27T17:12:00Z', and both JSON blob shapes ('error: {"auth": {"code": "resource_gone"}}' and 'auth: {"code":"resource_gone","hint":"send /new"}'). Quoted JSON keys never reach the assignment rules because the quote sits between the key word and the colon.

cases.angle: Task 2: the same diagnosis material placed AFTER an auth-ish key word.
cases.expectedBehavior: #14: only secrets are redacted; ordinary diagnostics must survive.
cases.observedBehavior: OVER-REDACTION, 13/13. 'auth: unauthenticated' -> 'auth: [redacted]'; 'auth_error: refresh_token_expired' -> 'auth_error: [redacted]'; 'credential: unrecoverable' -> 'credential: [redacted]'; 'authorization: insufficient_scope_for_this_operation' -> 'authorization: [redacted]'; 'auth_reason=configuration mismatch' -> 'auth_reason=[redacted] mismatch'; and token=<path>, auth_session=<uuid>, auth_session=<ULID>, token=<git SHA>, auth_at=<ISO timestamp>, authorization=<semver+build>, auth_attempts=999999999999, 'authorize: /Users/x/pkg/src/server.ts:113:9' all become '[redacted]'. The code comment declares this bias deliberate ('a secret delivered to a chat surface is far worse than a lost value'), so the value is a diagnosis-loss tradeoff rather than an accident — but the loss is total for the message half of the notice.

cases.angle: Task 3: the \b removal on the vendor-prefix rules — find legitimate text it now destroys (words containing sk_, sk-, rk_, pk_, or ey + two dotted segments).
cases.expectedBehavior: Ordinary diagnostic prose survives; only secret-shaped tokens are redacted.
cases.observedBehavior: DESTROYED, 13/13. 'disk_usage_exceeded: no space left on device' -> 'di[redacted]: no space left on device'; 'network_unreachable: dial tcp failed' -> 'netwo[redacted]: dial tcp failed'; 'task_execution_timeout after 300000ms' -> 'ta[redacted] after 300000ms'; also risk_assessment_failed, ask_permission_denied, task-runner-timeout, work_dir_missing, work_queue_stalled, apk_install_failed, TASK_EXECUTION_FAILED (the rule is /i), mask_pattern_invalid. The `ey` rule eats dotted symbol paths: 'at monkey_patch_util.test_module.expected_name (x.ts:1:1)' -> 'at monk[redacted] (x.ts:1:1)' and 'they_failed_here.module_name.function_call ...' -> 'th[redacted] ...'. Near misses survive only because their tail is under 8 chars ('fork_failed: EAGAIN', 'backpack_sync_error'). Real vendor keys and a real JWT still redact, so the rule is not simply broken — it is unbounded.

cases.angle: Task 3, escalated: the same rules run over the CODE field, which #14 says is the whole diagnosis.
cases.expectedBehavior: A runtime code reaches the operator and the channel intact; it is never sensitive.
cases.observedBehavior: TOTAL DIAGNOSIS LOSS for a plausible code family: code disk_quota_exceeded delivers '[turn failed] di[redacted]: startup failed'; task_execution_timeout -> 'ta[redacted]'; network_unreachable -> 'netwo[redacted]'; work_dir_missing -> 'wo[redacted]'; risk_check_failed -> 'ri[redacted]'. The five codes the contract names (the four rebindable ones plus rebind_cap_exceeded) are unaffected — by luck of spelling, not by design.

cases.angle: Task 4: several quoted pairs in one message, an unbalanced quote, nested quotes, a quoted value spanning a newline, and an empty quoted value.
cases.expectedBehavior: Each quoted secret is fully redacted; non-secret quoted values and empty values survive; no shape leaves secret material in the clear.
cases.observedBehavior: Correct for four shapes: several pairs -> 'api_key: "[redacted]" token: "[redacted]" note: "keep me"'; a value spanning a newline -> 'api_key: "[redacted]"'; the D2 whitespace case -> 'api_key: "[redacted]"'; empty values ('api_key: ""', "api_key: ''") untouched. FAILS OPEN for four shapes: an unbalanced quote ('api_key: "<secret> and then prose') ships the secret verbatim; nested single-in-double ('api_key: "it's <secret>"') ships it; nested double-in-single ("api_key: 'the \"<secret>\" value'") ships it; a mismatched pair ('api_key: "<secret>'") ships it. And 'api_key: "<secret1> and later token: "<secret2>"' produces 'api_key: "[redacted]"<secret2>"' — the match spans quote 1 to quote 2, so the PROSE and the second key name are erased while the second secret is delivered.

cases.angle: Task 5: does a NORMAL gjc turn stream end with a trailing newline, or is automatic replay effectively dead? Measured against the real binary, not assumed.
cases.command: gjc -p --mode json 'Reply with exactly the word: ok' > /tmp/g4-gjc-ok.out; gjc --resume 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000 -p --mode json hi; bun test /tmp/g4-pending.test.ts -t 'g4-5a'
cases.expectedBehavior: If real gjc output is newline-terminated, the pending guard costs nothing for a normal failing turn.
cases.observedBehavior: NOT a regression. Real gjc/0.15.3 `-p --mode json` emitted 21062 bytes / 14 frames (session, agent_start, turn_start, 3x message_start, 3x message_end, 3x message_update, turn_end, agent_end), ends with '}\n', and the fragment after the last newline is ''. Fed whole or one character at a time, GjcTurnStream.pending is false and finalText is set. The real FAILING shape (`gjc --resume <unknown-id>`) writes 0 bytes to stdout and a non-JSON stack trace to stderr, so pending is false there too. Automatic replay is alive.

cases.angle: Task 5: realistic ndjson — a message_end frame followed by a partial frame, and one with a clean trailing newline.
cases.expectedBehavior: pending is true only when a real partial frame is buffered.
cases.observedBehavior: message_end + clean newline -> false; message_end + a complete second frame -> false; message_end + trailing whitespace only -> false (the guard trims); empty stream -> false; message_end + '{"type":"tool_execution_start","na' -> true; a bare partial frame -> true. No false positive on any complete stream.

cases.angle: Task 5: does the guard refuse a replay for a normal failing turn?
cases.expectedBehavior: The realistic failing turn (empty stdout, error on stderr) is replayed; only a mid-write truncation is refused.
cases.observedBehavior: 'realistic failing turn: empty stdout, error on stderr' -> REPLAYED (2 turn spawns). A tool frame WITH a trailing newline -> NOT REPLAYED, '1 tool call(s)'. The same frame truncated mid-write -> NOT REPLAYED, 'an unterminated frame the child died mid-write'. message_end + a partial frame -> NOT REPLAYED, '7 output token(s), an unterminated frame the child died mid-write'. The guard costs a replay only in the mid-write case it was written for.

cases.angle: Task 6: fresh home must boot on defaults; chmod 000, a directory, a symlink to a missing target and a zero-byte file must be refused at BOOT.
cases.expectedBehavior: Absent -> defaults. Every shape that EXISTS but cannot be read or parsed -> refused.
cases.observedBehavior: fresh home -> BOOTED ON DEFAULTS (mentionAllowlist undefined). chmod 000 -> REFUSED config_invalid 'unreadable (EACCES)'. directory in its place -> REFUSED config_invalid 'unreadable (EISDIR)'. zero-byte file -> REFUSED config_invalid 'could not parse'. symlink to a missing target -> BOOTED ON DEFAULTS with mentionAllowlist=undefined: the read returns ENOENT, so a config.json that exists as a link with a deleted target is indistinguishable from no configuration and the gateway comes up with an open policy. That is the same absent-vs-unreadable fail-open the requireFile split was added to close, reached through a link instead of a mode bit.

cases.angle: Task 6: all five shapes at RELOAD must keep the previous config.
cases.expectedBehavior: ok:false with a config_invalid diagnostic and the previous config object retained, for every shape including the absent file.
cases.observedBehavior: All five returned ok:false with result.config === the live object (identity, not a copy) and mentionAllowlist ['owner'] / channels {c1:{engagement:'open'}} / debounceMs 1500 intact. Diagnostics: 'is missing' (absent), 'unreadable (EACCES)', 'unreadable (EISDIR)', 'is missing' (dangling symlink), 'could not parse' (zero-byte).

cases.angle: Task 6: prove the mention-gated room stays gated over the REAL unix socket for shapes gen-3 did not cover (EACCES and the dangling symlink).
cases.expectedBehavior: The verb replies ok:false config_invalid and the live allowlist is unchanged.
cases.observedBehavior: Both shapes: verb response {"ok":false,"diagnostics":[{"code":"config_invalid","message":"<home>/config.json is unreadable (EACCES)|is missing; keeping the previous configuration"}]}; a stranger's mention-gated group message was engaged=false before AND after the failed reload, and the allowlisted 'owner' was still engaged=true afterwards — so the retained policy is the real live one. The daemon logged 'gateway config reload (verb reload) FAILED; keeping the previous config: ...' in both runs.

cases.angle: Task 7: over the real unix socket with a real GjcClient, the four codes rebind and an unrelated code does not.
cases.expectedBehavior: resource_gone / spawn_failed / terminal_uncertain / managed_append_identity_mismatch each bump the epoch once with a log line carrying cause + both epochs + lifetime; unsupported_state_version bumps nothing and surfaces as a genuine failure with no /new hint.
cases.observedBehavior: Each of the four rooms reached epoch 1 with exactly one log line, e.g. 'gateway session rebind 1/3 origin=discord/channel/resource cause=resource_gone epoch 0 -> 1 (lifetime 1)' — same shape for spawn_failed, terminal_uncertain and managed_append_identity_mismatch. unsupported_state_version: epoch 0, zero log lines, and the delivered chat.message read exactly '[turn failed] unsupported_state_version: runtime says unsupported_state_version' with no '/new'.

cases.angle: Task 7: the cap fails explicitly on the 4th, the log line carries code + both epochs + lifetime, and the delivered notice carries code and message.
cases.expectedBehavior: Three rebinds then an explicit rebind_cap_exceeded, with the runtime's own code and message in the delivered notice.
cases.observedBehavior: epoch stopped at 3 with exactly three log lines: 'gateway session rebind 1/3 origin=discord/channel/caproom cause=resource_gone epoch 0 -> 1 (lifetime 1)', '2/3 ... epoch 1 -> 2 (lifetime 2)', '3/3 ... epoch 2 -> 3 (lifetime 3)'. Messages 1-3 delivered '[turn failed] resource_gone: the session endpoint record is gone Send /new to rebind this conversation.'; messages 4 and 5 delivered '[turn failed] rebind_cap_exceeded: rebind cap 3 reached after resource_gone at epoch 3 Send /new to rebind this conversation.'. The identical string was written to the operator log by the same call site.

cases.angle: Task 7: /new over the socket is the manual remedy the notice advertises.
cases.expectedBehavior: A capped origin that receives /new can rebind again; the epoch and the lifetime total both stay honest.
cases.observedBehavior: Four failing messages capped the origin at epoch 3 with a rebind_cap_exceeded notice. The allowlisted author's /new bumped the epoch to 4 and cleared the budget, and the next rebindable failure was allowed and logged 'gateway session rebind 1/3 origin=discord/channel/newroom cause=terminal_uncertain epoch 4 -> 5 (lifetime 4)' — consecutive counter reset to 1/3, lifetime correctly continued at 4.

cases.angle: Task 8: prove the epoch is bounded for a recurring turn-level failure whose replay succeeds (25 messages).
cases.expectedBehavior: At most cap=3 bumps; messages past the cap fail explicitly.
cases.observedBehavior: persistedEpoch=3 with exactly 3 log lines (1/3, 2/3, 3/3, lifetimes 1..3). m1-m3 returned the replayed reply; m4-m25 (22 messages) all threw RebindCapExceededError. A replayed turn provably does not restore the budget.

cases.angle: Task 8: report what the alternating fail/clean-turn pattern does (deliberately permitted).
cases.expectedBehavior: Per the declared design the cap does not bound this shape; the lifetime total must make the growth visible.
cases.observedBehavior: 12 rounds of (fail-then-successful-replay, then a fully clean turn) produced 12 rebinds and persistedEpoch=12 with zero cap rejections. Every consecutive counter read '1/3' — the cap never fires — while the lifetime totals ran 1..12, the last line being 'gateway session rebind 1/3 origin=discord:group:alternating cause=managed_append_identity_mismatch epoch 11 -> 12 (lifetime 12)'. Epoch grows at half rate (one bump per two messages) and is visible only through the lifetime field. Recorded as the permitted observation the design names, not a defect.

cases.angle: Task 8: a replayed turn must never clear the budget, or 8a's bound collapses.
cases.expectedBehavior: Three successful replays still leave the budget spent.
cases.observedBehavior: Three fail-then-replay turns each returned 'replayed' and consumed one slot (1/3, 2/3, 3/3); the fourth threw RebindCapExceededError with the epoch held at 3.

defects.title: The NON_SECRET_KEY denylist disarms the whole key=value gate: a real credential is delivered verbatim whenever the key name contains an exempt word
defects.contract: #14 'only SECRETS redacted' — the secret half of that obligation
defects.observed: '[turn failed] spawn_failed: expired_password=deadbeefcafebabe0123456789 Send /new to rebind this conversation.' — the secret in the clear. 18/18 exempt-word spellings leak, including max_token=, max_secret=, MAX_TOKEN=, AWS_MAX_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=, auth_expires_secret=, retries_token=, token_ttl_secret=, count_api_key=, age_token=, ms_token=, num_credential=, total_authorization=, remaining_secret=, window_passwd=, attempt_token=, seconds_apikey=, and the quoted form.
defects.expected: A credential-shaped value is redacted; an exempt key word may suppress redaction only for values that are actually quantities.
defects.impact: Under-redaction is the failure the previous gate was replaced to fix, and the replacement reintroduces it through a different door: the discriminator is now a 20-word hand-written list matched anywhere at an underscore boundary in the key. 'expired_token=', 'expired_password=' and 'attempt_token=' are ordinary auth-error vocabulary, so this is reachable from a real provider error blob. The value shape is ignored entirely, so no length or entropy check backs it up.
defects.test: /tmp/g4-redaction.test.ts 'g4-1c-DEFECT: an exempt NON_SECRET_KEY word anywhere in the key delivers a real credential verbatim'

defects.title: The \b removal on the vendor-prefix rules destroys ordinary diagnostics, including the runtime CODE that is the whole diagnosis
defects.location: packages/gateway/src/orchestrator/rebind.ts redactSecrets, the unanchored /(?:sk|rk|pk|...)[-_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}/gi and /ey[...]{8,}\.[...]{8,}\.[...]{8,}/ rules (introduced in 7954ff6 to fix generation-3 D1)
defects.contract: #14 'only SECRETS redacted; ordinary diagnostics must survive' and '#14 exists to remove the zero-diagnosis line'
defects.repro: formatFailureNotice(new GjcRuntimeError('w', { code: 'disk_quota_exceeded', message: 'network_unreachable: dial tcp failed' }))
defects.observed: '[turn failed] di[redacted]: netwo[redacted]: dial tcp failed' — both halves of the notice destroyed. 13/13 realistic diagnostic strings are damaged: disk_usage_exceeded, risk_assessment_failed, task_execution_timeout, ask_permission_denied, task-runner-timeout, network_unreachable, work_dir_missing, work_queue_stalled, apk_install_failed, TASK_EXECUTION_FAILED, mask_pattern_invalid, and any dotted symbol path whose first segment contains 'ey' ('at monkey_patch_util.test_module.expected_name' -> 'at monk[redacted]').
defects.expected: A prefix match should require that the surrounding token actually look like a key (e.g. a boundary plus a shape/entropy test), not redact any word containing 'sk_' followed by 8 characters. The comment claiming the unanchored rule 'can only over-redact a secret-shaped token' is false: 'network_unreachable' is not secret-shaped.
defects.impact: Worse than the leak it replaced for triage purposes: the fix traded a conditional secret leak for unconditional diagnosis loss on a whole family of plausible codes. The four rebindable codes and rebind_cap_exceeded escape only because of how they are spelled, so any new gjc code containing sk_/rk_/pk_ silently becomes an opaque line — precisely the ~2h-of-muteness failure #14 exists to eliminate.
defects.test: /tmp/g4-redaction.test.ts 'g4-3a-DEFECT ...' and 'g4-3b-DEFECT: a runtime CODE containing sk_/rk_ is destroyed ...'

defects.title: The quoted-value rule fails open on an unbalanced, nested or mismatched quote
defects.location: packages/gateway/src/orchestrator/rebind.ts SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_QUOTED (value class [^"']*, closing group \2) plus SECRET_ASSIGNMENT_BARE's exclusion of " and '
defects.repro: redactSecrets('api_key: "deadbeefcafebabe0123456789 and then prose') and redactSecrets(`api_key: "it's deadbeefcafebabe0123456789"`)
defects.observed: Both return the input unchanged — the secret is delivered in full. Same for a double-quoted secret inside single quotes and for a mismatched pair ('api_key: "<secret>\''). And 'api_key: "<s1> and later token: "<s2>"' returns 'api_key: "[redacted]"<s2>"': the quoted match spans quote 1 to quote 2, erasing the prose and the second key name while shipping the second secret.
defects.expected: An opening quote after an auth-ish key means everything up to the next quote OR the end of the line is a candidate value; a missing or mismatched closing quote must never mean 'redact nothing'.
defects.impact: A truncated or nested-quote runtime blob — the normal shape when a child is killed mid-write or when a provider embeds a quoted message — delivers the credential whole. The bare rule cannot rescue it because it excludes quote characters from the value class.

defects.title: Real diagnosis is erased whenever it follows an auth-ish key word: prose states, compound codes, paths, UUIDs, session ids, git SHAs, timestamps and versions
defects.location: packages/gateway/src/orchestrator/rebind.ts looksLikeCredential — value.length >= 12 is the only shape test
defects.contract: #14 'only SECRETS redacted — ordinary diagnostics must survive'
defects.observed: 'auth_error: [redacted]'. 13/13 cases lose their diagnosis: 'auth: unauthenticated', 'credential: unrecoverable', 'authorization: insufficient_scope_for_this_operation', 'auth_reason=configuration mismatch', token=<absolute path>, auth_session=<uuid>, auth_session=<ULID>, token=<git SHA>, auth_at=<ISO timestamp>, authorization=<semver+build>, auth_attempts=999999999999, 'authorize: /Users/x/pkg/src/server.ts:113:9'.
defects.expected: The declared contract sentence promises credential-shaped values only. A UUID, a path, a SHA and an English word are not credentials.
defects.impact: Diagnosis loss in the direction b83ad30 deliberately traded away ('a secret delivered to a chat surface is far worse than a lost value'), which is a defensible call for the value half — but the code comment's premise that 'the runtime CODE still carries the diagnosis either way' is exactly what G4-D2 breaks, so the two defects together can leave a notice with no diagnosis at all. Reported so the tradeoff is a decision rather than an accident.
defects.test: /tmp/g4-redaction.test.ts 'g4-2b-DEFECT: real diagnosis IS erased when it follows an auth-ish key word'

defects.title: A config.json symlinked to a deleted target boots on defaults, so the absent-vs-unreadable split still fails open at BOOT
defects.contract: Reload/boot contract: 'ENOENT means defaults at boot; anything else (EISDIR, EACCES, EIO) is a config file that EXISTS and cannot be read, which must never silently become a defaults-only open policy — not at reload, and not at boot either.'
defects.observed: BOOTED ON DEFAULTS with mentionAllowlist=undefined and channels=undefined, i.e. a mention-gated room becomes open. chmod 000 (EACCES), a directory (EISDIR) and a zero-byte file are all correctly refused; only the dangling symlink slips through because Bun.file(...).text() reports ENOENT for it.
defects.expected: A config.json that exists as a directory entry but cannot be resolved is an unreadable file, not an absent one. An lstat (or a readlink check) distinguishes them; the reload path is already correct because requireFile refuses every error.
defects.impact: Boot-time fail-open reachable by an ordinary operator layout (config.json symlinked into a dotfiles repo whose target moved or was deleted). It is exactly the hole the architect pass closed for mode/type errors, reached through a link. RELOAD is unaffected: all five shapes retain the previous config, proven over the real socket for two of them.
defects.test: /tmp/g4-config.test.ts 'g4-6a: boot refuses every unreadable shape but boots on a genuinely absent file'

observations: Task 5 answered in the negative: the pending guard is NOT a product regression. Real gjc/0.15.3 `-p --mode json` output is newline-terminated (14 frames, ends '}\n', empty trailing fragment) and a real failing `--resume` writes 0 bytes to stdout, so a normal successful-then-failing turn leaves no pending buffer and automatic replay stays alive. The guard only fires on a genuine mid-write truncation.

Task 8 alternating pattern (permitted by design): 12 rounds of fail-then-replay interleaved with clean turns produced epoch 12, 12 rebinds, zero cap rejections, every consecutive counter reading '1/3', and lifetime totals 1..12. The lifetime field is the only thing that makes this visible, and it does.
